regime_context: Detector shows a narrow one-narrative rotation: Banks (H + HK) is the sole eligible leader with the highest durability_bar (0.56), while Energy (H-shares) is the runner-up but not eligible (no absolute-trend gate pass). Gate_helps is true, so the absolute-trend discipline has historically reduced drawdown on HK sector history — but momentum rank itself is only a focus lens, and the Hurst tag on the leader is mean-revert, not trend.
emerging_watch: Watching whether Energy (H-shares) ever flips to eligible=true — the condition to retire this watch is Energy gaining eligible=true at a state refresh with durability_bar above 0.36 while Banks falls below eligible=true.

theses.subject: Banks (H + HK)
theses.thesis: Banks is the only theme with both a top momentum rank and an eligible absolute-trend gate pass. The one validated edge in this detector is drawdown/shake-out avoidance via the trend gate, and Banks is the only leader sitting on the right side of that gate. Durability_bar of 0.56 is the highest in the table, suggesting leadership has been persistent. I lean with the prevailing narrative but cap enthusiasm because the Hurst tag says mean-revert, not trend — leadership is attention-dominant, not alpha-carrying.
evidence: rank 1, score 1.188, eligible=true — only eligible theme at the top of the table
gate_helps=true — absolute-trend gate is the single validated risk-control edge, and Banks is on the eligible side
one_narrative_dominant=true, breadth_of_rotation frac=0.12 — leadership is narrow but concentrated
theses.dissent: Hurst tag mean-revert on the leader suggests momentum is unstable and may snap back; with rank-IC ~0, the top rank carries no independent return forecast, only a risk-on positioning stamp.

falsifier.text: Banks (H + HK) theme loses its eligible=true status at the next state refresh, or its score falls below the Energy runner-up's score.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable

theses.subject: Energy (H-shares)
theses.thesis: Energy is the challenger with score 0.98 but eligible=false — it fails the absolute-trend gate. Since the one validated edge is drawdown control via that gate, a non-eligible theme carries no discipline support to be overweight. This is not a fade call on a crowding flag; it is simply the absence of the only backtested protective leg.
evidence: hurst_tag='trend' — interesting, but gate is eligibility, not tag
gate_helps=true — the gate historically cuts volatility/drawdown; Energy sits outside it
theses.dissent: Energy is tagged 'trend' and breadth is 0.30, which could indicate genuine momentum not yet confirmed by the gate; if it crosses to eligible, the underweight lean loses its basis.

falsifier.text: Energy (H-shares) becomes eligible=true while its durability_bar holds above 0.36.

check.reason: theme has no scalar etf_proxy → not cleanly scorable
